text: Brother Jonathan in London (Milton Bradley, 1910)

Brother Jonathan, an enterprising Yankee, a little of a farmer, something of an inventor, and upon a pinch not a bad horse trader, had long entertained the idea he would like to visit London, and as he expressed it, see 'how they hitched up there.'
So one bright June day we find him in the 'money center of the world,' arranging for lodgings in a house not far from the British Museum.
Having deposited the contents of his valise and, as he expressed it, 'got the hang of the school house,' he started out saying he might as well take in what was nearest him.
He entered the area in front of the Museum where a policeman told him he could check his umbrella inside, and if he had [BLANK] he could leave that also.
Jonathan said 'he would not part with it for [BLANK].'
